Polysomnography Report
Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.

This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomnogram. Total sleep time was 345 minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%. Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, comprising only 10% of total sleep time.

Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. Those events were predominantly obstructive apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%. The patient's baseline oxygen saturation was 95%. No significant periodic limb movements were noted.

Impression: The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

Clinical History: 56-year-old female with a new 1.2 cm cystic or pleomorphic microcalcifications in the left breast at the 10 o'clock position, identified on screening mammogram (B-RADS 4C).

Diagnosis: Left Breast, 10 o'clock, Core Biopsy: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), intermediate nuclear grade.

Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled left breast core; one five tan-white, firm core biopsy, ranging from 10 cm to 1.5 cm in length. A routine radiograph confirms the presence of microcalcifications corresponding to the area of concern. The cores are submitted entirely in one cassette.

Microscopic Description: Sections show breast tissue with multiple ducts expanded and filled by a heterogeneous population of atypical epithelial cells. The architecture is predominantly solid and cribriform. The cells exhibit moderately enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei with irregular contours. Central necrosis (comedonecrosis) is present within some of the involved ducts, associated with prominent microcalcifications. No evidence of stromal invasion is identified in the tissue provided.

Comment: The findings are diagnostic of Ductal Carcinoma in Situ. This is a core biopsy diagnosis. Definitive grading and assessment of margins will be performed on the subsequent excision specimen. Radiologic-pathologic correlation is recommended.

Clinical History: 45-year-old female with a 2.5 cm solid, hypoechoic nodule in the right lobe of the thyroid, discovered on ultrasound.

Diagnosis: Thyroid, Right Lobe, Fine-Needle Aspiration; Suspicious for Malignancy (Bethesda Category VI)

Specimen Adequacy: The specimen is adequate for evaluation.

Microscopic Description: The aspirate is cellular and shows crowded clusters of follicular cells with a microfollicular architecture. Clinical History: 56-year-old female with a new 1.2 cm cluster of pleomorphic microcalcifications in the left breast at the 10 o'clock position, identified on screening mammogram (BI-RADS 4C).

Diagnosis: Left Breast, 10 o'clock, Core Biopsy: Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (DCIS), intermediate nuclear grade.

Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled 'left breast cores,' are five tan-white, firm core biopsies, ranging from 1.2 cm to 1.5 cm in length. A specimen radiograph confirms the presence of microcalcifications corresponding to the area of concern. The cores are submitted entirely in one cassette.

Microscopic Description: Sections show breast tissue with multiple ducts expanded and filled by a monotonous population of atypical epithelial cells. The architecture is predominantly solid and cribriform. The cells exhibit moderately enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei with irregular contours. Central necrosis (comedonecrosis) is present within some of the involved ducts, associated with psammomatous microcalcifications. No evidence of stromal invasion is identified in the tissue provided.

Comment: The findings are diagnostic of Ductal Carcinoma in Situ. As this is a core biopsy diagnosis, definitive grading and assessment of margins will be performed on the subsequent excision specimen. Radiologic-pathologic correlation is recommended.

Specimen: Left breast core

needle biopsy

For your information, a colonoscopy is a procedure that allows the physician to inspect the inside of the colon. The procedure is performed under sedation and is usually done in a hospital or clinic setting. The physician will insert a long, flexible tube called a colonoscope into the rectum and push it through the colon. The colonoscope has a camera and a light at the tip, which allows the physician to see the inside of the colon. The physician can take samples of tissue or polyps during the procedure. After the procedure, the patient may feel some bloating or gas, which is normal. The patient should avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity for a few days after the procedure. The patient should also avoid alcohol and caffeine for a few days after the procedure.
